title: Napkin: traffic heuristics & rollout sprint schedule (Mar 2026)
body:
Context / goal:
Quick sketch for the upcoming sprint release: migrate model-routing fallback to new policy, tune traffic shaping heuristics, and land observability hooks. Primary goal — validate rollback/mitigation paths under a staged traffic ramp with minimal customer impact.

Assumptions:
- Primary traffic mix: 70% short-gen (<=64 tokens), 30% long-gen (>=256 tokens) during peak.
- SLO targets unchanged: 95th <= 180ms for short-gen, 95th <= 600ms for long-gen for hosted tier.
- Dedicated pools reserved for canary hours (2 x p4d-equivalent).
- Feature flag gating available: ff:model-routing-v2 + ff:shortpath-cache.

Preflight checklist (quick napkin, expand later):
[ ] Confirm canaries: cohort size, endpoints, percent rules (JIRA-4872).
[ ] Reserve capacity: Dedicated pools + burst staging for 2h window. Ops ticket opened.
[ ] Instrumentation: streaming traces, token-level cost metrics, KV-cache hit rate, kernel selection logs.
[ ] Smoke tests: local perf harness + staged synthetic traffic for 30m.
[ ] Runbook: owner list, escalation phone numbers, slack-runbook pinned.
[ ] Rollback hooks: FF kill-switch, traffic-shift route to fallback model (small variant), automated circuit-breaker.
[ ] Alert thresholds codified in monitor runbook (see linked Confluence).

Sprint calendar (3-day mini-launch within sprint) — tentative:
Day -2 (Mon): dry run + synthetic spike (09:00-11:00). Validate KV-cache warming. Run smoke suite + perf regressions.
Day -1 (Tue): Canary rollout (09:00 start): 1% for 15m -> 5% 30m -> 10% 60m. Observe latency, error rate, OOM, GPU thermals.
Day 0 (Wed): Ramp window 08:00-12:00: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 3 hours, hold 30m at each step. If stable, flip secondary flags and run extended 2h soak at 50%.
Evening (Wed 18:00): Post-mortem sketch + immediate followups list.

Canary experiment plan (details to land):
- Cohorts: internal beta users + 5% random external (traffic tag).
- Metrics to watch (primary): 95th latency, p99 latency, request error rate (>0.5%), model-serve GPU memory growth, KV-cache hit delta, token-per-request cost change.
- Safety gate: any sustained p99 > baseline + 25% for 5 min -> automatic rollback to previous model variant.

Throttle curve sketches (operational knobs):
- Start: baseline concurrency 1000 / node.
- Soft throttle: reduce new long-gen to 20% of baseline once node GPU util > 75% for 2 consecutive mins.
- Hard throttle: divert all long-gen to fallback variant if OOMs observed or GPU util > 90% for 30s.
- Client-facing degrade: return short-response stub + retry header (X-RW-Retry) if heavy tail detected.

Rollback matrix (quick):
Trigger -> Action -> Owner
- Error rate spike (>1%): pause rollout, revert FF (Liam), notify SRE (Nadia)
- Latency regression (95th +30%): slow ramp, cancel next increase, run perf trace owner (Aisha)
- OOM / node crashes: immediate redirect to fallback pool, patch pod spec (Evan), escalate to on-call infra
- Observability missing: abort, revert, postmortem

Release notes draft (for product/marketing, pared-back):
- New: model-routing v2 introduces cost-aware routing which reduces avg token cost for short-gen by ~12% in internal tests. (Flagged: ff:model-routing-v2)
- Improved: better KV-cache warmup for bursty prefixes; decreases cold-start tail for common prompts.
- Ops: added token-level cost telemetry and per-route latency tracing.
- Breaking/Behavioral notes: if customers pin to a model variant id, routing v2 will not override pinned routes. No action needed.
- Known issues: rare cold-cache spike observed in synthetic long-gen tests (investigating).

Post-release checks (first 24h):
- 0-2h: validate canary cohort stability, paging on-call if thresholds breached.
- 2-6h: validate sampling telemetry, ensure cost delta within expected band.
- 6-24h: daily rollup snapshot and quick retro in #release-ops.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Decide final cohort selection: include region-specific canaries? (APAC?)
- Confirm exact dedicated capacity units and billing owner.
- Finalize alert runbook wording + SLAs for rollback triggers.
- Add short script to automate flag flip + traffic ramp (ops automation PR).

Notes to self / ragged edges:
- This is a napkin draft — will flesh into formal runbook with annotated playbook cards.
- Keep the initial ramp slow: field experiments show smaller steps reduce churn in background caching layers.
- Leave 1h buffer after major infra windows (DB migrations) — coordinate with infra calendar.

Links / refs (to copy into final):
- JIRA-4872: model-routing-v2 rollout epic
- PR: serving-runtime/pull/912 (kernel selection tweaks)
- Confluence: perf-telemetry-token-level (placeholder)

Owners (quick rota):
- Release lead: Liam Chen
- SRE / oncall liaise: Nadia Ruiz
- Observability / perf: Aisha Kumar
- Infra / rollback automation: Evan Patel

-- end napkin --
